pages.author: Scenario briefing · fictional
pages.subject: By Friday I’ll have finished it
paragraphs: Fictional event schedule: draft Tuesday; review Wednesday; final preparation takes about one working day after comments. Volunteers arrive Friday at 10 am. A brief welcome sheet can be prepared separately. New sections are outside the current estimate. Do not present a draft as an approved final pack.

pages.title: Can we promise Friday morning?
pages.instruction: Listen for the problem, the response and the next step

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: Can we promise the event pack will be ready by Friday morning?
lines.audioText: Can we promise the event pack will be ready by Friday morning?
lines.translation: Podemos prometer que o material do evento estará pronto na sexta de manhã?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: The draft will be ready on Tuesday, but we need the review before making that promise
lines.audioText: The draft will be ready on Tuesday, but we need the review before making that promise.
lines.translation: O rascunho ficará pronto na terça, mas precisamos da revisão antes de prometer

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: The review is booked for Wednesday. How long will the final changes take?
lines.audioText: The review is booked for Wednesday. How long will the final changes take?
lines.translation: A revisão está marcada para quarta. Quanto tempo levarão os ajustes finais?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: About one working day after the comments arrive, provided the brief doesn’t change
lines.audioText: About one working day after the comments arrive, provided the brief doesn’t change.
lines.translation: Cerca de um dia útil depois de receber os comentários, desde que o escopo não mude

lines.text: So by Thursday evening you’ll have finished the main version?

lines.text: That’s the plan. On Friday morning I’ll be checking the printed copies

pages.title: A commitment with conditions
pages.instruction: Listen for the problem, the response and the next step

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: I can do that. What would put the handover at risk?
lines.audioText: I can do that. What would put the handover at risk?
lines.translation: Posso fazer isso. O que colocaria a entrega em risco?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: A late review or a new section. We should flag either as soon as it happens
lines.audioText: A late review or a new section. We should flag either as soon as it happens.
lines.translation: Uma revisão atrasada ou uma nova seção. Devemos avisar assim que acontecer

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: Agreed. Let’s confirm the review, then communicate the deadline with that condition
lines.audioText: Agreed. Let’s confirm the review, then communicate the deadline with that condition.
lines.translation: Combinado. Vamos confirmar a revisão e comunicar o prazo com essa condição

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: And keep a short progress update, so nobody assumes a draft is the final version
lines.audioText: And keep a short progress update, so nobody assumes a draft is the final version.
lines.translation: E manter uma atualização breve para ninguém presumir que o rascunho é a versão final

pages.title: The review has slipped
pages.instruction: Listen for the new information and decide how to respond
pages.message: Hi, Ana. The draft is ready, but the review has moved from Wednesday to Thursday afternoon. The final changes still need roughly one working day after we receive the comments. That means we shouldn’t promise the final pack for Friday morning. We can have a short welcome sheet ready by ten, while the full pack is still being checked. Could you ask whether that would cover the volunteers’ immediate needs? If it does, we can agree a later handover for the complete version rather than quietly sending an unchecked draft. We also need to make clear that a new section would require another estimate
pages.audioText: Hi, Ana. The draft is ready, but the review has moved from Wednesday to Thursday afternoon. The final changes still need roughly one working day after we receive the comments. Could you ask whether that would cover the volunteers’ immediate needs? If it does, we can agree a later handover for the complete version rather than quietly sending an unchecked draft. We also need to make clear that a new section would require another estimate.
